title: Private jet operator safety audits: AOC, ARGUS, WYVERN, IS-BAO
description: What a private jet operator's certificate and safety audits mean: the AOC, ARGUS ratings, the WYVERN Wingman standard and IS-BAO, from the official sources.
h1: How to read an operator's safety credentials
lead: Every charter flight is flown by an operator, not by the broker. This guide explains the licence every operator must hold and the independent audits that go further, based on what the bodies that issue them publish.

sections.h: The licence: the Air Operator Certificate
p: The starting point is the operator's licence. As the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore explains it, {{audit.aoc_what}}. For a Singapore operator the rule is simple: {{audit.aoc_needed}}. The certificate is not a one-off: {{audit.aoc_oversight}}.

Other countries work the same way, each through its own authority. The certificate comes with operations specifications that list what the operator may do and with which aircraft, so we check that the aircraft offered for your trip is covered. The US regulator gives private customers the same advice we follow ourselves: {{audit.faa_ask_certificate}}.

sections.h: Independent audits: going beyond the licence
p: A licence shows that the authority has approved the operator. Independent audits look at how the operator actually runs its safety management, and they are voluntary. Three are widely used in business aviation.

ARGUS: {{audit.argus_who}}. It rates operators at several levels. {{audit.argus_gold}}. At a higher level, {{audit.argus_platinum_audit}}, and {{audit.argus_platinum_renewal}}. The top level is Platinum Elite: {{audit.argus_platinum_elite}}, and {{audit.argus_elite_cycle}}.
IS-BAO: {{audit.isbao_what}}. {{audit.isbao_icao}}. Registration has stages: {{audit.isbao_stage1}}, while {{audit.isbao_stage3}}. {{audit.isbao_audit}}, and {{audit.isbao_renewal}}.

We accept an operator without further approval only when the operator certificate that flies your trip holds a current ARGUS Platinum or Platinum Elite rating, WYVERN Wingman or Wingman PRO, or IS-BAO registration at its second or third stage. We check it in the auditor's own registry for every booking and keep the record with your trip.

Many good operators, above all in Asia and the Middle East, hold none of these audits. We use such an operator only after the owner of Archē Executive has approved it for your trip, after further checks of its certificate, insurance, history and crew, and only after we have told you in writing which audit it holds, or that it holds none.

For every operator, whatever its audit: two pilots on every jet flight; passenger liability insurance of at least fifty million US dollars for a jet and twenty-five million for a turboprop; and no fatal accident, serious incident or regulatory sanction in the last five years without a written explanation and the owner's approval. An operator involved in an accident or serious incident is suspended until we have reviewed it. Our booking system does not let a trip go forward until this record is complete.

sections.h: What we check before you see a quote
p: Before we propose an operator we check its certificate and the aircraft listed on it, its insurance, and its audit status with the audit bodies above.

Audit claims must be accurate. Under US rules, {{audit.us_no_false_audit_claims}}. We hold ourselves to the same standard everywhere: we only state an audit result we have checked with the audit body.

Who is the operator, and may I see its certificate? Is this aircraft on that certificate? Which independent audit does the operator hold, and when does it expire? A good broker answers all three in writing before you sign.

faq.q: Is an audited operator safer than one without an audit?
faq.a: An audit is an extra, independent check of how the operator manages safety. It does not replace the authority's licence, and no audit is a promise about a single flight. It is one of several things we weigh before proposing an operator.
No. We are a broker. Every flight is operated by a licensed operator, named in your quote and your charter agreement before you confirm.
